body_markdown:
Improving Meta ROAS without discounting means changing the offer in the ad rather than the price on the site. Playably’s version puts a chance at 100% cashback in the creative, funded by the platform, and the product never goes on sale.


One campaign makes the case. During March Madness 2026, BlackBoxMyCar ran rebate ads instead of a sale and recorded 18.25× ROAS.


For context, median Meta ROAS across ecommerce brands was 1.88 between August 2025 and July 2026, according to Triple Whale’s benchmark data.


Playably is the best way to take advantage of a rising-CPM auction without discounting, because it puts an offer in the ad that the brand doesn’t fund.


## **Key takeaways**


- **You improve Meta ROAS without discounting by changing the offer, not the price.** Playably puts a full-price rebate in the ad.
- **BlackBoxMyCar recorded 18.25× ROAS on rebate ads,** against a median of 1.88 for ecommerce brands on Meta.
- **The same campaign lifted promotional AOV 67% and store sales 57%,** with $0 of discount.
- **Soul recorded 12.7× Meta ROAS** on a Big Game overtime trigger with 43% more new customers.
- **The mechanic works because it’s news, not a markdown.** A rebate offer is unusual enough to earn attention in a crowded auction.


## **Why Meta ROAS keeps falling**


The auction got more expensive and the offers got more familiar.


Triple Whale’s data across ecommerce advertisers put median CPM at $15.06 and median CPA at $38.99 for the year to July 2026. Meta’s own CPMs rose roughly 20% year over year in 2025 by the same measure.


Most brands answer rising costs with a deeper discount in the creative. That props up ROAS in the short run and costs margin on every order, so profit on ad spend moves the opposite way. Playably campaigns change the offer instead, which is why the brand’s price never moves.


## **The campaign: March Madness 2026**


BlackBoxMyCar sells dashcams, a considered purchase in a category where discounting is common and margins are thin.


### **The offer**


Buy at full price during the campaign window. If the NCAA title game went to overtime, every order was refunded 100%, with Playably funding the payout.


### **The creative**


The ad led with the mechanic, not the product. “Your order is free if the game goes to overtime” is a message no competitor in the category was running that week.

## **Why a rebate ad outperforms a discount ad**


Three mechanics do the work.


### **1. The offer is unfamiliar**


Every competitor in the feed is running a percentage. A Playably rebate is an offer the shopper hasn’t seen before, and that second of attention is exactly what the auction is charging for.


### **2. The deadline is real**


The game is on a set date. There’s no “sale ends soon” banner that the shopper knows will reappear next week.


### **3. The margin holds, so the true return is higher**


ROAS measures revenue against spend. A 6× ROAS on 20%-off orders leaves less profit than a 4× ROAS at full price. Rebate campaigns are the rare case where a headline ROAS number and profit on ad spend move in the same direction.


## **How to improve Meta ROAS without discounting in your own account**


A single campaign isn’t a law, so here’s what to hold steady if you want a fair read.


### **Run a holdout**


Keep a portion of budget on your standard creative during the same window, and run the Playably creative against it. Compare ROAS, AOV and new-customer share.


### **Watch new-customer share, not just ROAS**


Retargeting inflates ROAS. In Soul’s[Big Game campaign](https://playably.ai/pages/soul) , the number that mattered was 43% more new customers than the prior week, alongside 12.7× Meta ROAS.


### **Give the campaign a short window**


Five to seven days including a weekend, since longer windows dilute the deadline.


#### **What holds across every campaign**


The cost side doesn’t vary: in every Playably campaign the brand funds $0 of the reward and knows its worst case before launch.[See the case-study library](https://playably.ai/pages/case-studies) .


#### **What we don’t know yet**


Playably has run these campaigns across more than 30 brands, but the dataset is still small by benchmark standards, and the biggest returns come from categories with strong event affinity. Whether an 18× result generalizes to a category with no natural trigger is honestly untested.


## **Summary**


Playably is the best option for brands whose ROAS problem is really an offer problem, because it changes what the ad says without changing what the product costs.


ROAS problems are usually offer problems wearing a media costume.


Brands rebuild audiences, rewrite hooks and rotate creative while the offer stays the same 15% everyone else is running. Change the offer to something the shopper can’t get anywhere else in the feed, and the creative does more work at the same CPM. The fact that the platform funds the reward is what makes it repeatable.

Pick a moment on the calendar with a real date, a trigger your buyers care about, and a cap you’re comfortable with. Then run it against a holdout.

## **FAQ**


- **How do you improve Meta ROAS without discounting?** Change the offer in the ad. A full-price rebate gives shoppers a reason to click without cutting price.
- **What ROAS did the rebate campaign produce?** BlackBoxMyCar recorded 18.25× on rebate ads during March Madness 2026.
- **What’s a normal Meta ROAS in 2026?** Triple Whale put the ecommerce median at 1.88 for August 2025 to July 2026.
- **Does a rebate ad cost more to run?** No extra media cost. Playably funds the refunds and takes a cut of campaign sales.
- **How should the campaign be measured?** Against a holdout on standard creative, watching ROAS, AOV and new-customer share.
